espn-603999.headline: Dupont at ten, with one training run, against South Africa
beats: France's captain Antoine Dupont has had one training run as emergency fly-half, the price of an injury crisis. The opponent has won the last five meetings in Paris, and France have beaten them once in their last ten.

The last meeting, on 8 November 2025, was a home defeat: France lost 17–32. Since then they have found their range, with eight tries against Fiji last weekend. South Africa put nine past Italy the same day, 66–7.
South Africa have been first in the world since 31 August, a place built on three home wins over New Zealand. Even a draw here hands it to New Zealand.
François Steyn, once of Racing 92 and Montpellier, reckons France have much more to lose. Against this opponent, in this city, they usually do.

espn-604000.headline: Argentina need a hooker, and Benetton have one
beats: Julián Montoya, 121 caps, is out for 12 days on HIA protocols after leaving early in Dublin. Leonel Oviedo, who replaced him, was also assessed, and Ignacio Ruiz is injured. So Argentina called up Bautista Bernasconi of Benetton, three caps, and Facundo Bosch, 35, who last played for them in 2021.

Italy have lost five straight and conceded 66, 57 and 47 in their last three. Their hooker, Tommaso Di Bartolomeo, says the plan is to put pressure on the scrum and the lineout. That is exactly where a borrowed hooker would feel it.
The shortage runs to the back. Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee against Ireland, and Santiago Carreras is out for the year.
Win, and Italy go up to 9th in the world, above Fiji and Wales. Fiji are their next visitors.

espn-604001.headline: New Zealand change eight and the tipsters don't blink
beats: Dave Rennie has made eight changes from the side that beat Scotland 43–21 and given Beauden Barrett the captaincy for the first time. Richie Mo'unga, back from injury, starts at 10.
Wales hosted New Zealand on this ground last November and conceded 52. They beat Japan 28–21 last weekend, having lost 0–43 to South Africa in July.
Steve Tandy has lost Aaron Wainwright to injury and wants his side to ignore the "aura". A Wales win would lift them above Fiji to 9th in the world.
The six SA Rugby tipsters all pick New Zealand, by between 20 and 40. The team sheet suggests Rennie agrees with them.

espn-604002.headline: England change ten and may still end the week top
beats: Steve Borthwick has made 10 changes to the side that beat Australia 45–22, forced by injuries and a few tired bodies. If France lose to South Africa on Friday, a win here could take England top of the North conference.

Will Joseph makes his first start, on the right wing, back in a Test squad for the first time since his debut in 2022. Max Ojomoh wins a third cap at inside centre, his first since being Man of the Match against Argentina in 2025. Borthwick has told them not to audition off script.

Japan have made one change: a debutant wing, Tokito. They lost by seven in Wales last weekend, and Eddie Jones promises "something a bit different" and a side that gets "quite dirty". Win by 16 or more and England drop below Scotland in the world rankings.
England have won all six previous meetings. New Zealand come to the same ground a week later, so the auditions have one Saturday to run.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland change seven. Fiji keep six.
beats: Dan Sheehan is out with concussion, so Tadhg Beirne captains Ireland for the first time. Sean Jansen's knee has ended his campaign, and Nick Timoney moves to number eight. Six of the starters still have more than 70 caps.

Fiji kept only six starters from the 54–17 loss in France. Josua Tuisova is back at centre, Ben Volavola starts at 10 and Peceli Yato captains from number eight, so the side that leaked 54 will at least look different.

Ireland ran in six tries against Argentina on 6 November, and Stuart McCloskey says they will not be drawn into an arm wrestle. Lose anyway and they fall to fifth in the world, behind France and England.
South Africa come to Dublin next. Fiji go to Italy, the only side below them in the table and the only other one still without a point.

espn-604004.headline: Both lost 21–43 to New Zealand. Someone must defend
beats: Australia lost 21–43 to New Zealand in October. Scotland lost by the same score to the same side at Murrayfield on 7 November, conceding seven tries and scoring nothing after half-time. Australia have since let in 45 at Twickenham.

Kyle Steyn says some of those seven tries came from first phase, and he wants "a real physical defensive performance" on Sunday. His other point was simpler: you cannot beat anyone while conceding 43. Both sides have tested it.

Scotland's captain, Sione Tuipulotu, learned the game in a Melbourne backyard against Isaac Kailea, now an Australia prop. Lose to his old opponent and Scotland drop below Australia to seventh in the world.
Ewan Ashman scored all three Scotland tries against New Zealand. Australia also scored three at Twickenham. Scoring has not been the problem.

espn-604005.headline: New Zealand need a 16-point win where they lost by 14
beats: England won the last meeting 33–19 at home, on 15 November 2025. Turn that round by 16 or more and New Zealand go top of the world rankings, above South Africa.

New Zealand have scored seven tries in each of their last three Tests, and kept Scotland scoreless after the break at Murrayfield. Beauden Barrett's two that day took him to 50 in Test rugby. Before this game he captains New Zealand for the first time, against Wales.
England arrive off a record win over Australia, 45–22 and seven tries. They will be without Alex Mitchell, facing a prolonged spell out after a hamstring operation.
Eddie Jones reckoned England might be distracted by New Zealand while they were still meant to be playing his Japan side. He was early, not wrong.

espn-604006.headline: Japan keep losing by a score. Scotland can't spare one
beats: Japan's last two defeats came by six and seven points: 28–34 to Fiji, then 21–28 in Wales. Before Edinburgh they go to Twickenham, where Eddie Jones wants 'the sky to fall in' against his old England side.
Scotland have conceded 43 twice this year, to Ireland and to New Zealand, and 38 in beating Argentina. The All Blacks coach still came away saying his side had been 'exposed' by Scotland at the maul.
A Japan win of any size drops Scotland below Australia in the world rankings. For a side that leaked 43 at Murrayfield last time out, a narrow margin is not guaranteed to fall their way.
Japan have nothing scheduled after this, so they have no reason to save anything.

espn-604007.headline: Ireland's scrum gets a rematch with the side that broke it
beats: South Africa won 24–13 at the Aviva Stadium last November, with a scrum penalty try and yellow cards for both Andrew Porter and Paddy McCarthy at the scrum. Porter did not play for Ireland again until Argentina this month, where he won a scrum penalty.

Dan Sheehan, captain while Caelan Doris is injured, is going through a 12-day return-to-play protocol after a concussion against Argentina. Sean Jansen's knee has ended his tournament, which leaves number eight open as well.

South Africa top the Nations Championship on points difference alone, ahead of New Zealand, and arrive having put 66 on Italy. An Ireland win would drop them to second in the world, behind New Zealand.
Against Argentina there were 11 scrums, and Ireland conceded no penalties at them. Against South Africa last November there were 20, and Ireland conceded six.

espn-604008.headline: Ninth in the world, decided by the bottom two
beats: Fiji are ninth in the world and Italy 11th, yet they are the only two sides in the Nations Championship without a point. Win in Udine and Italy go up to ninth, above Fiji and Wales.
Italy have lost five straight and conceded 66 at home to South Africa on 7 November. Fiji beat Japan 34–28 in October, then let in 54 away to France.
Both have a game first. Italy host Argentina in Genoa, and Fiji go to Dublin, where Jake White has Josua Tuisova back in the centres and Caleb Muntz on the bench.
Italy's next Test after this is Scotland in February. Fiji's is Spain at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to sit on a loss.

espn-604009.headline: Argentina stand between France and the Twickenham final
beats: France top the North by two points from England, and North 1st meets South 1st in the grand final at Twickenham. This is their last pool game. They come to it straight after hosting South Africa on the same ground, with an injury crisis Fabien Galthié could do without.

France have scored at least six tries in each of their last three, the latest 54–17 against Fiji. Argentina's last outing in Europe was a 42–12 defeat to Ireland, and they have Italy in Genoa before they reach Saint-Denis.
Even a draw would drop France below England to 5th in the world rankings, which is a lot to give up to a side with one win this year.
Argentina's only result since July that was not a defeat was 28–28 with Australia. Australia are the side a point above them in the South.

espn-604010.headline: Australia have shipped 138 in three Tests. Next, Cardiff
beats: Australia are 7th in the world, three places above Wales, and below them in the Nations Championship all the same. The 138 came from 50 and 43 against New Zealand, then 45 in England.

Wales beat Japan 28–21 with four tries. In July they scored nothing in South Africa. Tomos Williams has started 12 of 13 Tests under Steve Tandy, and his replacements have had 48 minutes in those 12. Tandy admits "there probably is an over-demand on Tomos".
Win, and Wales go up to 9th while Australia drop below Argentina, the side they could only draw with in September.
Wales go to France in February. Australia's next fixture is Hong Kong at the World Cup in October 2027, which leaves a long time to sit on 138.
